## Investigation

What can the legitimate, already-installed official configuration application do
while offline, and what does it add beyond the preserved controller baseline?

::: {.manual-prereq title="Preserve the pre-Dashboard baseline"}

Confirm that the power-cycle record exists and that the Mac remains offline.
Use only an already installed, legitimately obtained application. Do not sign
in, update, install, flash firmware, or apply a device setting in this stage.
The active specification must explicitly permit observation of Dashboard.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Create the application observation record"}

Copy the template:

```bash
cp evidence/templates/dashboard-offline.yml evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-dashboard-offline.yml
```

Record the application name/version, launch result, authentication prompt (if
any), visible device state, and which controls are visible or disabled. Treat a
login prompt as an observation; do not attempt to bypass it.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Close without applying changes"}

Close the application without selecting a configuration control. Reconfirm the
ordinary MIDI behaviour from Stage 3. This establishes whether observation alone
changed the baseline.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Evaluate application dependency"}

Record Dashboard as offline-capable only for actions actually observed to work
offline. Record it as authentication-dependent only when a prompt prevented a
named action. Neither outcome determines whether the controller itself works
offline.

:::
